evidence_spans: On each C1, ForeSight replays the CTAs with its queueing model, whereas Accel-Sim simulates the trace cycle by cycle, and GCoM and AMALI analyze the trace of every warp. ForeSight is faster than all three, with a median of 26 s on one CPU core to predict a workload on one C1, against 1272 s for Accel-Sim and 40 s and 108 s for GCoM and AMALI.

extra_quotes: Our evaluation on hardware configurations of nine NVIDIA GPUs shows that ForeSight predicts kernel execution time with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 8.3%, compared with 14.1% for the best baseline.
It runs 49× faster than the cycle-level simulator Accel-Sim and faster than interval-based models such as GCoM.
With the aid of ForeSight, we explore configurations derived from the H20 GPU for LLM inference and find one with 1.78×its performance/cost.
On some MIG instances and on another GPU, vLLM selects a different kernel or grid for a workload, and we evaluate only the workloads whose kernel and grid stay the same.
